expression_system: HEK293 cells transiently transfected with the OAT cDNA vs mock-transfected controls; 2-min uptake of [14C]PFOA
measurement_type: Km/Vmax (Michaelis-Menten, non-linear least squares), [14C]PFOA varied 5-400 uM
direction_reabsorption_or_secretion: secretion (basolateral uptake into the proximal tubule cell)
source_table: Table 1 (full text) | Vmax/Km = 9.99 uL/min/mg protein, computed here
assay_volume_note: TABLE 1 UNITS DEFECT: the third column is headed "Km/Vmax (ul/mg protein/min.)" and prints 0.10. The number is Km/Vmax, but ul/mg protein/min are the units of Vmax/Km. The intrinsic clearance here is Vmax/Km = 9.99 uL/min/mg protein. Taking the printed value as a clearance is wrong by a factor of ~100 and reverses the ranking: by the printed column rOAT3 looks highest, by clearance it is the lowest. Human and rat orthologues measured in the SAME expression system, which is the only way to compare species without also changing laboratory. Human/rat clearance ratio is 1.21 on OAT1 and 1.78 on OAT3, against a roughly 50-fold species difference in half-life -- the paper's own conclusion is that species differences in renal elimination are NOT attributable to OAT affinity
